No code, no backend needed \u2014 just a live site on your own kodely.site URL in minutes.", "targetKeyword": "build a portfolio website with AI", "category": "Use Cases", "bodyHtml": "

What a good portfolio website actually needs

Before you open any tool, it helps to know what a portfolio site is actually for: giving someone 30 seconds to decide you're worth a longer look. That means a handful of things matter far more than clever design tricks.

  • Work samples or case studies. Not just a logo grid \u2014 a few pieces with enough context that a stranger understands what you did and why it mattered.
  • An about section. Who you are, what you do, and what you're looking for. Two or three paragraphs is plenty.
  • A way to get in touch. Email, a contact form, or both. Make it impossible to miss.
  • A link to your resume or CV. Recruiters and clients both look for this first, especially on mobile.

Get those four right and the rest \u2014 color palette, fonts, layout \u2014 is polish. Get them wrong and no amount of polish saves the site.

The one-prompt approach

The fastest way to build a portfolio site with Kodely is to describe the whole thing in one message: who you are, what you do, the sections you want, and the tone you're going for. Kodely reads that description and generates a complete site around it \u2014 structure, copy placeholders, and layout \u2014 in one pass, then shows you a live preview of the actual app as it's built.

You don't need to plan every section in advance. A rough, specific description beats a vague, exhaustive one. Name your field, mention two or three real projects, and say what you want visitors to do when they land on the page.

A real example prompt

Here's a prompt you can copy and adapt for your own portfolio:

"Build a portfolio website for me, a freelance product designer named Priya Shah. I want a hero section with my name, a one-line tagline about designing fintech products people actually trust, and a button to view my work. Below that, a projects section with three case studies: a banking app redesign, a budgeting tool for freelancers, and a checkout flow for an e-commerce client \u2014 each with a short description and the outcome. Then an about section with two paragraphs about my background in design systems and accessibility. Then a contact section with my email and a link to download my resume. Use a clean, minimal style with a lot of white space and one accent color, a deep teal."

Prompts like this work well because they give Kodely real content to build around \u2014 actual project names, a real accent color, a specific tone \u2014 instead of leaving every decision generic.

What Kodely actually generates

This is the part worth understanding clearly: Kodely doesn't produce a mockup or a page of raw HTML. It generates a real Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 application, built from a foundation codebase with hand-built UI primitives \u2014 Button, Card, Section, Nav \u2014 that your site's components are assembled from. Every section you asked for becomes an actual .tsx component file.

You can open the code view in-app at any point and read or copy the real source files Kodely generated. There's no zip download or project export today \u2014 if you want the files, you copy them from the code view \u2014 but what you're looking at is genuine, working code, not a rendered image of one.

Customizing via chat

Once the first version exists, refine it the same way you built it: describe the change in chat. "Make the hero shorter," "swap the accent color to navy," "add a fourth case study for the checkout redesign" \u2014 Kodely edits the real components behind the scenes rather than starting over.

Every successful generation is saved as a checkpoint, so if a change doesn't land the way you wanted, rolling back to the previous version is free. That makes it safe to experiment \u2014 try a bolder layout, see how it looks, and revert in one step if it doesn't work.

Publishing to a live URL

When you're happy with the site, one click publishes it to a real public address at yourname.kodely.site \u2014 free, included, with no separate hosting step to set up. Every publish is automatically scanned for accidentally-leaked secrets or API keys before it goes live, so you're not shipping something you'd regret.

Kodely doesn't support custom domains yet, so your site lives at a kodely.site subdomain rather than a domain you own \u2014 worth knowing going in if you were planning to point a domain you already have at it.

FAQ

Do I need to know how to code?

No. You describe the site and the changes you want in plain English. If you're curious, the code view lets you see and copy the real component files Kodely generates, but you never have to touch them.

Can I use my own domain for my portfolio?

Not yet. Published sites live at a free yourname.kodely.site address. Custom domain support isn't available today.

Can I download the project files?

Not as a bundled export right now. You can view and copy the generated source files individually from the in-app code view.

How much does building a portfolio site cost?

Kodely runs on credits tied to real AI cost. A first build typically runs 100\u2013150 credits, and a follow-up change is usually in the same range. New accounts get 750 credits free, no card required, which covers a first build with room for several rounds of edits. If a build fails to compile, you're not charged for it \u2014 Kodely attempts one automatic repair first.

Can I keep changing the site after I publish it?

Yes. Publishing doesn't lock the project. Keep describing changes in chat and republish whenever you're ready \u2014 there's no extra step and no separate hosting to manage.
